===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|id=rule|:inh|enm:lawe|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|lawe}}, {{m|enm|laȝe}}, from {{inh|en|ang|lagu|t=law}}, borrowed from {{der|en|non|lǫg|t=law|lit=things laid down or firmly established}}, originally the plural of {{m|non|lag||layer, stratum, a laying in order, measure, stroke}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*lagą|t=that which is laid down}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*legʰ-|t=to lie}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|law|t=law}}, {{cog|is|lög|t=things laid down, law}}, {{cog|fo|lóg|t=law}}, {{cog|no|lov|t=law}}, {{cog|sv|lag|t=law}}, {{cog|da|lov|t=law}}, {{cog|fi|laki|t=law}}. Compare typologically distant cognate {{m+|ru|уложе́ние}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|ǣ}} and {{m|ang|ġesetnes}}. More at {{l|en|lay}}.

Not typically thought to be related to {{m|en|legal}}, nor to {{ncog|fr|loi}}, {{ncog|es|ley}}, as these all derive from {{ncog|la|lēx}}, ultimately from {{ncog|ine-pro|*leǵ-|t=to gather}}; however, see {{l|la|lēx}} for an alternative theory that indeed links it to the same {{m+|ine-pro|*legʰ-}}. In any case, {{m-self|en|law}} is the inherited {{w|Germanic}} term whereas {{m|en||leg-}} is {{lg|borrowed}} via Latin and {{cog|roa|-}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|usually with "the"}} The [[body]] of [[binding]] [[rule]]s and [[regulation]]s, [[custom]]s{{,}} and [[standard]]s [[establish]]ed in a [[community]] by its [[legislative]] and [[judicial]] [[authority|authorities]].
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=XLIV|page=361|passage=Not unnaturally, "Auntie" took this communication in bad part.{{...}}Next day she{{...}}tried to recover her ward by the hair of the head. Then, thwarted, the wretched creature went to the police for help; she was versed in the '''law''', and perhaps had spared no pains to keep on good terms with the local constabulary.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1941|author=w:George Orwell|title={{w|The Lion and the Unicorn: Socialism and the English Genius|The Lion and the Unicorn}}|section=Pt. I
|passage=Here one comes upon an all-important [[English]] trait: the respect for constitutionalism and legality, the belief in "the '''law'''" as something above the State and above the individual, something which is cruel and stupid, of course, but at any rate ''incorruptible''. It is not that anyone imagines the '''law''' to be just. Everyone knows that there is one '''law''' for the [[rich]] and another for the [[poor]]. But no one accepts the implications of this, everyone takes it for granted that the '''law''', such as it is, will be respected, and feels a sense of outrage when it is not.}}
#: {{ux|en|The courts interpret the '''law''' but should not make it.}}
#: {{ux|en|In theory, [[entrapment]] is against the '''law'''.}}
## The [[body]] of such rules that [[pertain]] to a particular [[topic]].
##: {{ux|en|property '''law'''}}
##: {{ux|en|commercial hunting and fishing '''law'''}}
## [[common law|Common law]], as [[contrast]]ed with [[equity]].
# A [[binding]] [[regulation]] or [[custom]] [[establish]]ed in a [[community]] in this way.
#: {{ux|en|There is a '''law''' against importing wallabies.}}
#: {{ux|en|A new '''law''' forbids driving on that road.}}
#: {{ux|en|The court ruled that the executive order was not '''law''' and nullified it.}}
#* {{RQ:Birmingham Gossamer|chapter=I|passage=As a political system democracy seems to me extraordinarily foolish,{{nb...}}. My servant is, so far as I am concerned, welcome to as many votes as he can get.{{...}}I do not suppose that it matters much in reality whether '''laws''' are made by dukes or cornerboys, but I like, as far as possible, to associate with gentlemen in private life.}}
# {{lb|en|more generally}} {{n-g|A [[rule]], such as:}}
## Any [[rule]] that must or should be [[obey]]ed, concerning [[behaviour]]s and their [[consequence]]s. {{q|Compare {{m|en|mores}}.}}
##: {{ux|en|"Do unto others as you wish them to do unto you" is a good '''law''' to follow.}}
##: {{ux|en|the '''law''' of self-preservation}}
## A [[rule]] or [[principle]] regarding the [[construction]] of [[language]] or [[art]].
##: {{ux|en|the '''laws''' of playwriting and poetry}}
## A [[statement]] (in [[physics]], etc) of an ([[observe]]d, [[establish]]ed) [[order]] or [[sequence]] or [[relationship]] of [[phenomena]] which is [[invariable]] under certain [[condition]]s. {{q|Compare {{m|en|theory}}.}}
##: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:law of nature}}
##* {{RQ:New Yorker|date=March 2, 1992|author=Richard Preston|url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/1992/03/02/the-mountains-of-pi|title=The Mountains of Pi
|passage=Observing [[pi]] is easier than studying physical phenomena, because you can prove things in mathematics, whereas you can't prove anything in physics. And, unfortunately, the '''laws''' of physics change once every generation.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260907201851/https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/1992/03/02/the-mountains-of-pi|archivedate=7 September 2026}}
##: {{ux|en|the '''laws''' of thermodynamics}}
##: {{ux|en|Newton's third '''law''' of motion states that to every action there is always an equal and opposite reaction.}}
##: {{ux|en|This is one of several '''laws''' derived from his general theory expounded in the ''Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica''.}}
## {{lb|en|mathematics|logic}} A [[statement]] (of [[relation]]) that is [[true]] under [[specified]] [[condition]]s; a [[mathematical]] or [[logical]] [[rule]].
##: {{ux|en|Mathematical '''laws''' can be proved purely through mathematics, without scientific experimentation.}}
## Any [[statement]] of the [[relation]] of [[act]]s and [[condition]]s to their [[consequence]]s.
##: {{ux|en|the '''law''' of scarcity}}
##: {{ux|en|the '''law''' of supply and demand}}
## {{lb|en|linguistics}} A [[sound law]]; a regular change in the [[pronunciation]] of a language.
##: {{ux|en|Grimm's '''law'''}}
##: {{ux|en|Dahl's '''law'''}}
## {{lb|en|cricket}} One of the [[official]] rules of [[cricket]] as [[codified]] by the its (former) [[govern]]ing [[body]], the [[MCC]].
# The [[control]] and [[order]] [[bring about|brought about]] by the [[observance]] of such rules.
#: {{ux|en|They worked to maintain '''law''' and order.}}
#: {{ux|en|It was a territory without '''law''', marked by violence.}}
# {{lb|en|informal}} A [[person]] or [[group]] that act(s) with [[authority]] to [[uphold]] such rules and order (for example, one or more [[police]] [[officer]]s).
#: {{ux|en|Here comes the '''law''' — run!}}
#: {{ux|en|then the '''law''' arrived on the scene}}
# The [[profession]] that deals with such rules (as [[lawyer]]s, [[judge]]s, [[police officer]]s, etc).
#: {{ux|en|He is studying for a career in '''law'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|She has practiced '''law''' in New York for twenty years.}}
# [[jurisprudence|Jurisprudence]], the [[field]] of [[knowledge]] which [[encompass]]es these rules.
#: {{ux|en|She went to university to study '''law'''.}}
# [[litigation|Litigation]]; [[legal]] [[action]] (as a [[means]] of [[maintain]]ing or [[restore|restoring]] [[order]], [[redress]]ing [[wrong]]s, etc.).
#: {{ux|en|They were quick to go to '''law'''.}}
# {{lb|en|now|uncommon}} An [[allowance]] of [[distance]] or [[time]] (a [[head start]]) [[give]]n to a [[weak]]er ([[human]] or [[animal]]) [[competitor]] in a [[race]], to make the race more [[fair]].
# {{lb|en|aviation}} A [[mode]] of [[operation]] of the [[flight control]]s of a [[fly-by-wire]] [[aircraft]].
#: {{ux|en|normal '''law'''; alternate '''law'''; direct '''law'''}}
# {{lb|en|fantasy}} One of two [[metaphysical]] [[force]]s [[rule|ruling]] the [[world]] in some [[fantasy]] [[setting]]s, also called {{m|en|order}}, and opposed to [[chaos]].
# {{lb|en|legal|chiefly|historical}} An [[oath]] [[sworn]] before a [[court]], especially [[disclaim]]ing a [[debt]]. {{q|Chiefly in the phrases "{{m|en|wager of law}}", "{{m|en|wage one's law}}", "{{m|en|perform one's law}}”, "{{m|en|lose one's law}}".}}

Cognate with {{cog|sco|lauch|t=one's tavern-reckoning or one's share of the cost, a score; a payment for drink or entertainment}}, {{cog|enm|lai|t=one's share of expenses, one's bill or account}}.
